chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, and I was present, about the Ethiopian chicken (Turkey), that it is brought out from the Haram. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not fly on its own.'
ai.seo_question: Can turkey be slaughtered inside the Haram in Mecca according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permitted slaughtering the Ethiopian chicken (turkey) within the Haram boundaries, basing his ruling on its inability to fly independently, which distinguishes it from birds that soar high and are thus excluded. This specific criterion highlights the Shia juristic focus on the physical capabilities of the animal rather than its species alone, ensuring that the sanctity of the Haram is maintained while allowing for the consumption of permissible poultry.
